Protected health information includes many common identifiers (e.g., name, address, birth date, Social Security Number) when they can be associated with the health information listed above."

subject sex specification.description: A subject sex is the phenotypic sex of given subject (human or animal) related to a given investigation, study, and/or specimen.

specimen collection site land use.description: Human use of land involving the management and modification of natural environment or wilderness into built environment.

the Global Microbial Identifier Minimum.description: The Global Microbial Identifier "Minimum data for Matching" (MDM) standard is a standard that defines essential contextual data fields to be included in genomic sequence repository records.

nitrate concentration.description: An environmental datum which describes the concentration of nitrate of a sample.

stream order categorical measurement dat.description: Stream order is a measure of the relative size of streams (The smallest tributaries are referred to as first-order streams, while the largest river in the world, the Amazon, is a twelfth-order waterway).

bacteria density.description: An environmental datum which describes the number of bacteria in a sample.

PFGE secondary test.description: Second PFGE pattern from given diagnostic restriction enzyme

MLST clonal complex.description: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) is a technique in molecular biology for the typing of multiple loci. The procedure characterizes isolates of microbial species using the DNA sequences of internal fragments of multiple housekeeping genes. Sequence types are grouped into clonal complexes by their similarity to a central allelic profile (genotype). As such, clonal complexes represent sequence types that share a number of identical alleles e.g. 5/7

MLST sequence typing.description: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST) is a technique in molecular biology for the typing of multiple loci. The procedure characterizes isolates of microbial species using the DNA sequences of internal fragments of multiple housekeeping genes. For each housekeeping gene, the different sequences present within a bacterial species are assigned as distinct alleles and, for each isolate, the alleles at each of the loci define the allelic profile or sequence type (ST).

core genome fingerprinting assay.description: The process of fingerprinting the core genome of a bacteria.

16S rRNA sequencing.description: 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing is a sequencing method used to identify and compare bacteria present within a given sample. 16S rRNA gene sequencing is a well-established method for studying phylogeny and taxonomy of samples from complex microbiomes or environments that are difficult or impossible to study.

Stx toxin type datum.description: A pathogenic shiga toxin produced by STEC E. coli.

Stx1 Toxin PCR result.description: A qPCR measurement result of Stx1 gene amplification.

Stx1 cell culture level.description: A measurement datum which describes the level of Stx1 toxin derived tissue culture toxicity.

Stx2 Toxin PCR result.description: A qPCR measurement result of Stx2 gene amplification.

Stx2 cell culture level.description: A measurement datum which describes the level of Stx2 toxin derived tissue culture toxicity.

AccuProbe Listeria monocytogenes culture.description: An AccuProbe reagent kit for identifying Listeria monocytogenes.

AccuProbe test result.description: A categorical diagnostic result of an AccuProbe test.

ribotyping.description: Ribotyping involves the fingerprinting of genomic DNA restriction fragments that contain all or part of the genes coding for the 16S and 23S rRNA. By digesting the genes with a specific restriction enzyme, fragments of different lengths are generated. By performing a Gel electrophoresis with the digested samples, the fragments can be visualised as lines on the gel, where larger fragments are close to the start of the gel, and smaller fragments further down. After blotting onto a matrix and probing, these lines form a unique pattern for each species and can be used to identify the origin of the DNA, almost like a barcode can identify a product.

riboprinting.description: This method is based on restriction endonuclease digestion of bacterial chromosomal DNA, followed by Southern hybridization to probes for sequences in the regions of bacterial DNA coding for the 5S-16S-23S (the Escherichia coli rrnB rRNA operon) rRNA operon. The probes have been developed that are directed to highly conserved regions of the rRNA operon present in all eubacteria and can therefore be used for ribotyping most bacteria

Qualicon (DuPont) RiboPrinter Microbial.description: A device that generates an automated genetic fingerprint of a bacterium from a bacterial suspension.

DuPont identification pattern library.description: A dataset which is a library of RiboPrinter recognised patterns.

RiboPrinter DUP Number.description: DuPont identification number from the DuPont identification library

RiboPrinter DUP similarity.value: The identification of an isolate was determined when the corresponding patterns matched one of the patterns of the DuPont Identification library of the RiboPrinter1 with a similarity of >0.85. The similarity threshold for an isolate joining a ribogroup is an adaptive value between 0.90 and 0.96, depending on the size of the ribogroup.
RiboPrinter DUP similarity.description: Similarity of pattern to one of the patterns of the DuPont Identification library of the RiboPrinter

sequencing chemistry.description: A laboratory sequencing datum which describes the method and chemistry used to determine the order of nucleotides in a DNA molecule.

read length.description: A datum of the number of base pairs per read.

sequencing run multiplex identifiers.description: Molecular barcodes, called Multiplex Identifiers (MIDs), that are used to specifically tag unique samples in a sequencing run. Sequence should be reported in uppercase letters

sequencing run sample identifier.description: A sequencing run sample identifier is an alphanumeric identifier for a sample. In bioinformatics processing this identifier is assigned to a sample in order to track it through the process of sequencing and analysis.

sequencing kit.description: Pre-filled, ready-to-use reagent cartridges. Used to produce improved chemistry, cluster density and read length as well as improve quality (Q) scores. Reagent components are encoded to interact with the sequencing system to validate compatibility with user-defined applications.

sequencing kit version.description: A string datum which is the version/configuration of the reagent cartidge.

adapter sequence.description: Adapters provide priming sequences for both amplification and sequencing of the sample-library fragments. Both adapters should be reported; in uppercase letters

read adapter trimming.description: The removal of adapter sequences from demultiplexed data reads

library preparation kit (GENEPIO_0000085.description: Packaged kits (containing adapters, indexes, enzymes, buffers etc), tailored for specific sequencing workflows, which allow the simplified preparation of sequencing-ready libraries for small genomes, amplicons, and plasmids.

number of expected base pairs per genome.description: The estimated size of the genome prior to sequencing. Of particular importance in the sequencing of (eukaryotic) genome which could remain in draft form for a long or unspecified period.

number of reads passing filter.description: Raw data are filtered to remove any reads that do not meet the overall quality as measured by a chastity filter. The chastity of a base call is calculated as the ratio of the brightest intensity divided by the sum of the brightest and second brightest intensities. Clusters passing filter are represented by PF in analysis reports. Clusters pass filter if no more than one base call in the first 25 cycles has a chastity of < 0.6.

sequencer flow cell cluster density.description: Cluster Generation is a process by which libraries amplified into clonal clusters on a flow cell. The density of those clusters in the lane, is the cluster density.

phred quality score.description: An assembly quality control datum that describes the quality of the identification of nucleobases generated in sequencing, where the score is logarithimically related to the probability of an error in base calling.

assembly method.value: the GROUP: MIxS term encompasses assembly method; estimated error rate; method of calculation
assembly method.description: Assembly method refers to how the reads were assembled into contigs for which either a de novo or mapping (reference based) strategy is used.

assembly status.description: An assembly quality control datum that describes the status of the assembly which is categorised from draft to finished.

read coverage.description: Coverage (read depth or depth) is the average number of reads representing a given nucleotide in the reconstructed sequence.

contig count.description: A contig count is the count of contigs that belong to a sequence assembly.

assembly name (identifier).description: Name/version of the assembly provided by the submitter that is used in the genome browsers and in the community

genome annotation source.description: For cases where annotation was provided by a community jamboree or model organism database rather than by a specific submitter

IRIDA case ID.description: An IRIDA case ID is a tracking identifier for a case used in the IRIDA.ca software system. It is used to cross-reference anonymized IDs.

draft data standard.description: The 'draft data standard' class contains draft representations of formal or defacto third party standards and related components. These representations may have been crafted without any involvement of related standards issuers and so no guarantee can be provided about their currency, accuracy or veracity.

I2B2 Data Protection role standard.description: The I2B2 Workbench Data Protection role standard is a standard which names and lists data protection roles between a user and a given dataset that define the level of detail a user has access to.

subject health status (GSCID-BRC).description: A description of whether a given subject organism appeared healthy, sick or deceased at the time of specimen extraction. If sick or deceased, additional details should be provided in project-specific fields.

GSCID-BRC Core Sample standard.description: The GSCID-BRC Core Sample Standard is an extension of the GMI MDM data standard

GSCID-BRC Core Project standard.description: A Core Project item is a field in the GSCID/BRC Project and Sample Application Core Project Standard.

Currently this distinguishes between "clinical or host associated" specimens and "environmental/food or other pathogen" specimens.

subject age - unit.description: Age unit of the age measurement of a subject (individual organism).

NCBI standard.description: The National Center for Biotechnology Information offers standards for submitting genomic project data to their BioProject and BioSample databases.

specimen collection location - country.description: The country of the site of a given specimen collection event.

travel end date.description: The date of a person's return to some residence from a journey originating at that residence.

infection aquired during travel.description: Infection aquired during travel is a boolean datum indicating a diagnosis of a traveller's infection during a given trip.

draft pathogenic epi case food record.description: A description of a food item that a case patient has come in contact with.

epidemiology contact network model.description: An epidemiology contact network model is a definition of the information necessary to connect pathogen transmission patterns between individuals or animals in connection with an outbreak investigation.

epi contact network model - human.description: An epi contact network - human is contact information about a person who may be involved in transmitting a pathogen.

epi contact network model - animal.description: This is a model that provides location and transportation information about an animal that may be involved in transmitting a pathogen to a human or other animal.

draft pathogenic epi case travel record.description: A record of a patient's recent travel - departure and return, mode of travel and locations visited - as it may pertain to an outbreak pathogen transmission event.

draft WGS lab sequencing quality metrics.description: A data specification which records the sequencing quality datum of a draft whole genome sequencing product.

human to human exposure process.description: A process in which one or more humans may be exposed to one or more contagious human infectious disease carriers.

PFGE pattern.description: A visual pattern caused by DNA fragments concentrated in stratefied bands in a Pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) gel plate.

outbreak exposure event location.description: A type of built structure that is suspected to be related to an outbreak investigation.

data specification.description: A data specification is a specification of a data structure that can hold a categorical, textual or numeric variable, or that has such variables or other data structures as component parts.

specimen history item.description: A specimen history item is a time-related datum about a particular specimen

host (common name).description: A host field which describes the commonly used name of the host.

host (scientific name).description: A host field which describes the taxonomic or scientific name of the host.

host health state.description: A host field which describes the health status of the host at the time of sample collection.

host health status details.description: A host data field which describes additional information pertaining to the health or disease status of the host at time of collection.

host health outcome.description: A host data field which describes the disease outcome in the host.

host disease.description: A host data field which describes the name of the disease experienced by the host.

host age.description: A host data field which describes the age of the host at the time of sampling.

host age unit.description: A host data field which describes the units used to measure the host's age.

host age bin.description: A host data field which describes the age category of the host at the time of sampling.

host gender.description: A host data field which describes the gender of the host at the time of sample collection.

host residence geo loc name country.description: A host geographical location field which describes the country where the host resides.

host residence geo loc name state provin.description: A host geographical location field which describes the state or province or territory of residence of the host.

host subject id.description: A host data field which describes the unique identifier by which each host can be referred to.

symptom onset date.description: A data field which describes the date on which the symptoms began or were first noted.

signs and symptoms (GENEPIO_0001400).description: A data field which describes the perceived change in function or sensation (loss, disturbance or appearance) indicative of a disease, reported by a patient.

preexisting conditions and risk factors.description: A data field which describes a medical condition that existed prior to the current infection (pre-existing condition) or a variable associated with an increased risk of disease or infection (risk factor).

complications.description: A data field which describes medical complications that are believed to have occurred as a result of host disease.

host vaccination information field categ.description: A data field category which refers to host vaccination information fields.

host vaccination status.description: A data field which describes the vaccination status of the host.

number of vaccine doses received.description: A data field which describes the number of doses of the vaccine received by the host.

host exposure information field category.description: A data field category which refers to host exposure information fields.

location of exposure geo loc name countr.description: A geographical data field which describes the country where the host was likely exposed to the causative agent of the illness.

destination of most recent travel city.description: A geographical data field which describes the name of the city that was the destination of most recent travel.

destination of most recent travel state.description: A geographical data field which describes the name of the province that was the destination of most recent travel.

destination of most recent travel countr.description: A geographical data field which describes the name of the country that was the destination of most recent travel.

most recent travel departure date.description: A date field which describes the date of an individual's most recent departure from their primary residence (at time of data collection) on a journey to one or more other locations.

most recent travel return date.description: A date field which describes the date of an individual's most recent return to some residence from a journey originating at that residence.

travel history.value: PCDS: Canada, Vancouver; USA, Seattle; Italy, Milan
travel history.description: A data field which describes an individuals travel history in last six months.

exposure event.description: A data field which describes an event leading to exposure.

exposure contact level.description: A data field which describes the exposure transmission contact type.

host role.description: A data field which describes the role of the host in relation to the exposure setting.

container record.description: A container id is an identifier that refers to a container object about a patient specimen. Container ids are referenced in clinical patient records reported to be suspect, or lab test results.

exposure setting.description: A data field which describes the setting leading to exposure.

strain identifier.description: A strain identifier is the unique microbial or eukaryotic strain name from a reference database that a sample has been matched to.

line list object.description: A line list is a collection of suspected or known disease outbreak cases. It may also include details about healthy patients associated with an exposure event (picnic, concert etc.) who have been interviewed in order to compare food intake, assess risk factors, etc. Note that the health status of people associated with an exposure event can change from healthy or unknown status, to ill patient.

exposure details.description: A data field which describes additional host exposure information.

awaiting ontology review.description: This class is a temporary holding bin for items that need a class hierarchy home, definition, and/or subclass items. Some classes have subclasses that are currently disjoint in other ontologies like ENVO, so awaiting resolution on such issues.

host reinfection information field categ.description: A data field category which refers to host reinfection information fields.

prior sarscov2 infection status.description: A data field which describes whether there was prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.

prior sarscov2 infection isolate ID.description: A data field which describes the identifier of the isolate found in the prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.

prior sarscov2 infection date.description: A prior infection data field which describes the date of diagnosis of the prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.

prior sarscov2 antiviral treatment.description: A data field which describes whether there was prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) treatment with an antiviral agent.

prior sarscov2 antiviral treatment agent.description: A data field which describes the name of the antiviral treatment agent administered during the prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.

prior sarscov2 antiviral treatment date.description: A data field which describes the date treatment was first administered during the prior Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.

sequence information field category.description: A data field category which refers to sequencing information fields.

exposure group healthy count.description: The count of healthy individuals or animals on a certain date/time from a group that was likely exposed to a pathogen

exposure group ill count.description: The count of ill individuals or animals on a certain date/time from a group that was likely exposed to a pathogen

purpose of sequencing.description: A data field which describes the reason that the sample was sequenced.

purpose of sequencing details.description: A data field which describes the description of why the sample was sequenced providing specific details.

sequencing date.description: A date field which describes the date the sample was sequenced.

library id.description: A data field which describes user-specified identifier for the library prepared for sequencing.

amplicon size.description: A data field which describes the length of the amplicon generated by polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification.

library preparation kit (GENEPIO_0001450.description: A data field which describes the name of the library preparation kit used to generate the library being sequenced.

flow cell barcode.description: A data field which describes the barcode of the flow cell used for sequencing.

sequencing instrument.description: A data field which describes the model of the sequencing instrument used.

sequencing protocol name.description: A data field which describes the name and version number of the sequencing protocol used.

sequencing protocol.description: A data field which describes the protocol used to generate the sequence.

sequencing kit number.description: A data field which describes the manufacturer's kit number.

amplicon pcr primer scheme.description: A data field which describes the specifications of the primers (primer sequences, binding positions, fragment size generated, etc.) used to generate the amplicons to be sequenced.

bioinformatics and QC metrics field cate.description: A data field category which refers to bioinformatics and quality control (QC) metrics fields.

raw sequence data processing method.description: A data field which describes the method used for raw data processing such as removing barcodes, adapter trimming, filtering etc.

dehosting method.description: A data field which describes the method used to remove host reads from the pathogen sequence.

consensus sequence name.description: A data field which describes the name of the consensus sequence.

consensus sequence filename.description: A data field which describes the user-defined filename of the FASTA file.

consensus sequence filepath.description: A data field which describes the filepath of the consensus sequence file.

consensus sequence software name.description: A data field which describes the name of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

consensus sequence software version.description: A data field which describes the version of the software used to generate the consensus sequence.

breadth of coverage value.description: A data field which describes the percentage of the reference genome covered by the sequenced data, to a prescribed depth.

depth of coverage value.description: A data field which describes the average number of reads representing a given nucleotide in the reconstructed sequence.

depth of coverage threshold.description: A data field which describes the threshold used as a cut-off for the depth of coverage.

r1 fastq filename.description: A data field which describes the user-specified filename of the read 1 (r1) FASTQ file.

r2 fastq filename.description: A data field which describes the user-specified filename of the read 2 (r2) FASTQ file.

r1 fastq filepath.description: A data field which describes the filepath of the read 1 (r1) FASTQ file.

r2 fastq filepath.description: A data field which describes the filepath of the read 2 (r2) FASTQ file.

fast5 filename.description: A data field which describes the user-specified filename of the FAST5 file.

fast5 filepath.description: A data field which describes the filepath of the FAST5 file.

number of base pairs sequenced.description: A data field which describes the number of total base pairs generated by the sequencing process.

consensus genome length.description: A data field which describes the file size of the assembled genome described as the number of base pairs.

ns per 100 kbp.description: A data field which describes the number of N (unidentified nucleotide) symbols present in the consensus fasta sequence, per 100kbp of sequence.

reference genome accession.description: A data field which describes the persistent, unique identifier of a genome database entry.

exposure event end.description: A date-time datum that marks the end of possible human or animal exposure to a pathogen agent, directly or indirectly.

exposure event start.description: A date-time datum that marks the start of a human or animal exposure event to a suspected pathogen agent, directly or indirectly.

bioinformatics protocol.description: A data field which describes the name and version number of the bioinformatics protocol used.

notification date.description: A notification date is the date that an outbreak is suspected by a laboratory or other agency and is reported per outbreak detection guidelines.

outbreak date.description: An outbreak date is on which disease onset appears to have occured

outbreak over.description: An outbreak over date is the date on which a disease outbreak appears to have abated

lineage and variant information field ca.description: A data field category which refers to lineage and variant information fields.

lineage/clade name.description: A data field which describes the name of the lineage or clade.

lineage clade analysis software name.description: A data field which describe the name of the software used to determine the lineage/clade.

lineage clade analysis software version.description: A data field which describes the version of the software used to determine the lineage/clade.

variant designation.description: A data field which describes the variant classification of the lineage/clade.

variant evidence.description: A data field which describes the evidence used to make the variant determination.

variant evidence details.description: A data field which describes the evidence used to make the variant determination.

diagnostic pcr protocol.description: A data field which describes the name and version number of the protocol used for diagnostic marker amplification.

diagnostic pcr ct value.description: A data field which describes the Ct value result from a diagnostic SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR test.

contributor acknowledgement field catego.description: A data field category which refers to contributor acknowledgement information fields.

data authors.description: A data field which describes the names of individuals contributing to the processes of sample collection, sequence generation, analysis, and data submission.

dataharmonizer provenance.description: A data field which describes the DataHarmonizer software and template version provenance.

data enumeration.description: A data item that is a set of entities, referenced by mention, that don't necessarily have something in common.

signs and symptoms (GENEPIO_0001523).description: An analytic datum which describes the observed or detectable signs, and experienced symptomps of an illness, injury, or condition.

food specimen datum.description: A particular attribute (feature, quality or process history) of a food sample.

food specimen specification.description: A food specimen type is a categorization of a food specimen, by the organism it is or came from, or by a class of food products.

disease cluster notification agency.description: An agency that has reported a disease cluster.

exposure group unknown health status cou.description: The count of individuals or animals for which no health status is available on a certain date/time from a group that was likely exposed to a pathogen.

person role.description: A role which inheres in a person and is realized by the process of being in the context of civilization

exposed person role.description: An exposed person role is the role a person takes on who has been exposed to a pathogen. In serious situations this may call for special treatment, e.g. quarantine.

resolving health trend.description: To restore to the normal state after some pathologic process.

assembly genome size.description: The assembly genome size is the sum of all lengths of a sequence assembly's contigs.

reference genome identifier.description: Identifier for a reference genome (used to build or compare an assembly) that is used in the genome browsers and in the community

genome size delta ratio.description: The 'genome size delta ratio' is a ratio of the difference between a sample's genome assembly size and the size of a given reference genome, over the reference genome size. The formula: | (reference_genome_size - assembly_genome_size) | / reference_genome_size This yeilds a decimal / percentage ranging from 0 = exact length, to say .1 which is equivalent to a 10% variance. If the ratio is too far from a quality control ratio that depends on the species in question, this indicates a bad assembly or a mis-identified sample.

genome size delta ratio QC threshold.description: This is the upper acceptable limit of the 'genome size delta ratio' with respect to a particular species. For Salmonella a 0.10 variance in length between an assembly size and a reference genome size may be acceptable. For E-coli a more generous 0.30 or .40 variance should be allowed, given the pathogenic subspecies’ highly dynamic genome.

contig N50 length QC threshold.description: The contig N50 length QC threshold is a minimum length threshold that a contig N50 length datum should be above for good QC. A lower length is indicative of assembly problems (insufficient read depth) or a mismatched reference genome.

contig N99 length QC threshold.description: The contig N99 length QC threshold is the minimum length that a contig N99 or NG99 length datum can be for satisfactory QC. This threshold avoids having too many gene coding regions prematurely clipped inside short contigs. An assembly having 1% or more of its content in less than 2Kbp chunks is cause for concern. Bacterial genes are generally about 1Kbp in length.

subject organism (host) taxonomic specie.description: The species of the host organism from which a specimen (pathogen) organism was obtained. Use the full taxonomic name, eg, "Homo sapiens".

assembly quality control datum.description: A single datum having to do with a metric for genomic sequence assembly quality control. A "quality control measurement" can be defined as a measurement that has some norm within a definable context, e.g. for a certain subspecies. It may be a calculated quantity. A "quality control metric" is an upper or lower bound threshold that a measurement is compared to. Surpassing the threshold may indicate an error situation. A "measure" can indicate an amount of activity, consumption, transformation, etc. but doesn't itself convey an over-stepping of bounds in the way that a metric does.

contig N99.description: The N99 length definition is identical to the N50 definition except that the threshold for determining the contigs is 1% of the nucleotides. This contig basepair length can be compared to a minimum threshold to determine if gene annotation (where contigs greater than say 2000bp are necessary) would generally succeed.

contig count QC threshold.description: The upper threshold of contig counts that are acceptable in a genome assembly. This may vary based on the overall genome length and depth of coverage. A large contig count may indicate insufficient read coverage.

project relevance.description: Indicates how the knowledge derived from the project can be applied, and to what field(s).

monoisolate sample scope.description: A monoisolate sample scope involves specimens from a single animal, cultured cell-line, inbred population, or possibly a heterogeneous population when a single genome assembly is generated from a pooled sample because multiple individuals are needed to collect enough material and an inbred line is not available; however, this situation is not preferred.

multiisolate sample scope.description: A multiisolate sample scope contains multiple individuals that represent distinct specimen collections, a population (representative of a species).

multispecies sample scope.description: A multi-species sample scope involves a sample representing multiple species.

environment sample scope.description: An environment sample scope indicates that the species content of the sample is not known. Generally, nucleic acid is directly isolated from an environmental sample for analysis. This is used for metagenome studies.

synthetic sample scope.description: A synthetic sample scope involves a sample synthesized in a laboratory.

other project objective.description: Other project objective: specify an objective not listed above

whole genomic data capture.description: Whole: the project makes use of the whole sample material (most common case). Use this for whole genome sequencing studies, transcriptome studies that are not targeting specific loci, epigenetic studies of a genome, and metagenomes or unbiased transcriptome studies of metagenomes.

raw sequence read objective.description: A raw sequence reads project objective has the goal of submission of raw reads to SRA or Trace repositories

sequence project objective.description: A sequence project objective has a goal of submission of sequence data to standard archival sequence databases (yielding accession.version identifiers; e.g., whole genome shotgun, cDNA sequences, transcript shotgun assemblies)

analysis objective.description: An "analysis project objective" indicates there was an other analysis not otherwise indicated, includes submission of BAM files.

sequence variation project objective.description: Variation: identification of sequence variation data for submission to dbSNP or dbVAR

epigenetic markers objective.description: DNA methylation, histone modification, chromatin accessibility datasets

transcript or protein expression objecti.description: Expression: assays of transcript or protein existence or abundance

mapping objective.description: Maps: non-sequence based map data; e.g., genetic, radiation hybrid, cytogenetic, etc.

array project method.description: Select Array if that is the primary method and no sequence data is submitted

mass spectrometry project method.description: Select Mass Spectrometry if that is the primary method

investigation datum.description: A categorical investigation datum is a datum pertaining to some entity examined for scientific research or diagnostic purposes and which has a scope that is broader than one of the clinical, environmental or epidemiological domains.

commensal role.description: An organism and its host share physical space but no evidence exists to determine if one benefits from this arrangement.

subject age.description: An age measurement datum which is the age since birth of a given organism that is involved in an investigation or study at a given time.

subject description.description: A subject description is a field containing additional information about an organism (related to an investigation, study and/or specimen) that is not included in other defined vocabulary fields.

host profile or identifers.description: The host profile or identifiers text is the "identification or description of the specific individual from which this sample was obtained".

subject identifier.description: A subject identifier is an identifier of a subject organism within the context of a particular investigation, study, or specimen extraction event.

subject disease.description: A name of disease in a subject that is related to a given investigation, study and/or specimen.

missing.description: A categorical choice recorded when a measurement value was known to be recorded in the past but the observed value cannot be located or retrieved for some reason.

not applicable.value: 'not applicable' is an appropriate value for the measure of femur length for a patient with a missing limb
not applicable.description: A categorical choice recorded when a measurable datum does not apply to a given context.

not collected.description: A categorical choice recorded when a datum was not measured with respect to some entity during some process.

subject disease stage.description: A subject disease stage is a measure of the acuteness of a subject organism's diagnosed disease, if any, at a given time in an investigation, study or specimen extraction event.

contig length QC threshold.description: A 'contig length QC threshold' is an integer setting which can be applied by an algorithm to an array of assembly and annotation contig lengths to remove (filter out) all items less than the threshold value. The reduced array is used for calculation of statistics.

contig NG50.description: The NG50 length is the same as the N50 length except that the length of the reference genome is used in the calculation rather than the assembly genome size.

contig length.description: A contig length is the count of base pairs in a given sequence assembly contig.

contig L50.description: An assembly quality control datum which is defined as number of contigs equal to or longer than the contig N50, when the assembly itself is factored into the calculation.

contig LG99.description: The LG99 count is like the L99 count except that the length of the reference genome is used in the calculation rather than the sum of assembly contig lengths.

animal body product.description: A product of an animal, as in blood, feces, sputum, etc. that has no particular anatomical site

antigenic formula.description: An antigenic formula is a string composed of codes representing categorized results of tests performed on various viral, bacterial or immune cell surface antigens.

specimen organism taxonomy (species).description: This is the taxonomic species descriptor of a specimen isolate (an organism found within a specimen.)

identifier model.description: An identifier moe3l indicates an identifier, the organization it has been issued by, and the status of the identifier - whether it is a primary one, active or archaic.

curator organization name.description: The curator organization name is the name of an organization that manages a given repository of entities (samples, isolates, sequences ...)

isolate identifier.description: An isolate identifier is an identifier assigned to a given isolate by a particular agency that is handling or storing it.

identifier status.description: An identifier status describes the principle role of an identifier assigned to an entity by its curator or handler. An entity may have a number of identifiers assigned to it over time. An identifier may be phased-out as can happen when its content is transferred to another curator.

data protection role.description: A data protection role is a role (or user permission) that a user has with respect to particular data.

original submission.description: An identifier used in the initial submission of content to a repository.

INSDC institution code.description: An INSDC institution code is an identifier of an organization from a list of sequence repository organizations managed by INSDC.

previous (archaic) identifier.description: An identifier that had been used previously but is no longer promoted.

geographic location datum.description: A geographical location datum is a datum that refers to a real, hypothesized or fanciful spatial location

draft NCBI BioSample geo_loc_name model.description: Geographical origin of the sample; use the appropriate name from this list http://www.insdc.org/documents/country-qualifier-vocabulary. Use a colon to separate the country or ocean from more detailed information about the location, eg "Canada: Vancouver" or "Germany: halfway down Zugspitze, Alps"

case identifier.description: A case ID is a unique identifier associated with a particular episode of care for an individual or animal.

neuter.description: An animal that has had a substantial part of its reproductive organs removed surgically.

pooled male and female.description: A phenotypic sex quality 'pooled male and female' is a categorical value used when the male and female categories or levels of a factor are combined. If used to describe a single organism, then the organism will be one or the other.

in process.description: A categorical choice recorded while the data for a given measurable datum has not finished being collected, is awaiting a conclusion, or has not yet been communicated.

INSDC standard.description: The International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC) is a long-standing foundational initiative that operates between DDBJ, EMBL-EBI and NCBI. INSDC covers the spectrum of data raw reads, though alignments and assemblies to functional annotation, enriched with contextual information relating to samples and experimental configurations.

not provided.description: A categorical choice indicating that information of an expected format was not given a value may be given at the later stage.

contact specification - address.description: The address component of a contact specification.

laboratory sequencing datum.description: A datum related to the sequencing assay process applied to an isolate.

test specification.description: A lab test specification indicates the inputs and outputs (results / conclusions) of a test.

subgroup.description: Taxonomy below subspecies; sometimes used in viruses to denote subgroups taken from a single isolate.

viral subtype.description: A viral subtype is a classification name for a virus according to some protocol.

phage type specification.description: An integer and character referring to a pattern of opaque or confluent lysis caused by a panel of bacteriophage infections e.g. 14a.

NCBI culture collection.description: An NCBI culture collection is a composite identifier containing “institution code:collection code”.

NCBI specimen voucher.description: The NCBI specimen voucher is an identifier composed of “institution code:collection code:specimen id” parts. In addition to a specimen identifier, it includes an institution-code (and optional collection-code) taken from a controlled vocabulary maintained by the INSDC that denotes the museum or herbarium collection where the specimen resides.

subject organism common name.description: The natural language (non-taxonomic) name of the type of organism (human or animal) that is the subject of a given investigation, study and/or specimen.

pH measurement.description: A data field which describes the DataHarmonizer software and template version provenance. In chemistry, pH is a numeric scale used to specify the acidity or basicity(alkalinity) of an aqueous solution

assembly and annotation project objectiv.description: The assembly and annotation objective is the set of objectives that assembly and annotation techniques (including instruments and software platforms) applied to a sample are meant to satisfy. This impacts on the quality control thresholds applied to the sequencing project.

draft GenEpiO component record.description: This class contains components under development for fulfilling GenEpiO and other standard data specifications. Components are relevant to epidemiological, laboratory, clinical or environmental pathogen sample data collection and analysis.

subnational region.description: A subnational region is a type of subnational entity similar to a nation's state, province, or territory.

public health data standard.description: A data standard related to public health research and service delivery.

reagent derived material from specimen.description: Reagent: material studied was obtained by chemical reaction, precipitation.

proteome data derived from specimen.description: Proteome material is protein or peptide sequences.

purified chromosome from specimen.description: Purified chromosome: one or more chromosomes or replicons were experimentally purified.

Targeted Locus Loci data capture.description: TargetedLocusLoci: capturing specific loci (gene, genomic region, bar code standard).

random survey data capture.description: Sequences generated from a random sampling of the collected sample; not intended to be comprehensive sampling of the material

contact specification.description: This is a collection of various human (and animal contact location) contact information specifications used in data standards.

1 - standard draft.description: Standard draft: describing the minimum information needed for submission to a public database.

2 - high quality draft.description: High quality draft: describing sequences with little to no manual review.

3 - improved high quality draft.description: Improved high quality draft: in which data is either reviewed by people or machines to some extent to indicate that most of the genetic data is assembled correctly, but some errors may still be present.

4 - annotation-directed improvement.description: Annotation-directed improvement: in which genetic information in various gene regions is represented as accurately as possible.

5 - non-contiguous finished.description: Non-contiguous finished: which includes sequences that have been reviewed by both people and machines and would be considered complete except for “recalcitrant regions” that are proving problematic for genome closure.

6 - finished.description: Finished: which describes un-gapped complete sequences that have minimal errors, if any. The biology of the microbe will determine whether this finished genome consists of more than one chromosome.

contig NG99.description: The NG99 length is the same as the N99 length except that the length of the reference genome is used in the calculation rather than the sum of assembly contig lengths.

contig LG50.description: An assembly quality control datum which is defined as number of contigs equal to or longer than the contig N50, when the genome size is factored into the calculation.

contig L99.description: Contig L99 is the number of contigs equal to or longer than contig N99. The length of the assembly itself is used in the calculation.

subject age at time of specimen collecti.description: A subject age at time of specimen extraction is the age (since birth) of the organism at the time a given specimen was extracted.

draft tuberculosis contextual data stand.description: The draft tuberculosis contextual data standard is a data standard for the collection of contextual information of a given tuberculosis case that pertain to typing, clinical treatment, and potential research questions.

draft PulseNet Canada Salmonella submiss.description: The PulseNet Canada Salmonella submission standard details the fields required in a PuseNet Canada pathogen submission report for Salmonella in spreadsheet format

PFGE Xbal pattern.description: A PFGE pattern resulting from DNA fragmentation induced by the Xbal enzyme.

PFGE Blnl pattern.description: A PFGE pattern resulting from DNA fragmentation induced by the Blnl enzyme.

National Laboratory for Enteric Pathogen.description: An NLEP ID is a unique identifier code for a sample registered with the Canadian "National Laboratory for Enteric Pathogens" (NLEP)

upload modified date.description: Date an uploaded sample was re-uploaded or had its metadata modified.

travel destination.description: A travel destination is a destination city (or populated place of some scale) which a given human has travelled to on a particular trip.

symptom duration.description: A symptom duration is a date-time entity which is the duration (in hours or days or weeks etc.) that one or more symptoms persist for in a particular human or animal

specimen collection location - city.description: The city where a specimen was collected (taken) from a subject or environment

genus of pathogen.description: This is the genus-level taxonomic name of an organism playing a pathogen role

species of pathogen.description: This is the species-level taxonomic name of an organism playing a pathogen role

symptom cessation date.description: A symptom cessation date is a date-time entity that marks the end of one or more reported symptoms pertaining to an episode of human or animal illness

specimen datum.description: This is a catch-all category for listing specimen related terms

data obfuscated.description: The 'data obfuscated' role between a user and given data entails that the user is authorized to see particular fields that have been transformed consistently such that statistics performed on those fields would yeild the same results as statistics applied to the un-obfuscated data. The purpose of obfuscation is to prevent related individuals or organizations from being identified.

data aggregated.description: The 'data aggregated' role between a user and given data entails that the user is authorized to see aggregated results (like the patient count) via preset reports, queries or views. The results are not obfuscated.

limited data set.description: A 'limited data set' role between a user and given data entails that a user is authorized to see some of the fields but the remainder are withheld (or encrypted).

de-identified data.description: A 'de-identified data' role between a user and given data entails that the user is authorized to see only those fields (including those that are encrypted) which do not contain information that could be use to identify particular individuals (whether patients or medical practitioners) or potentially organizations in the case where an investigation may implicate them.

data protected.description: A 'data protected' role between a user and given data entails that a user must be authorized in order to view that data.

specimen collector.description: A datum containing the name of persons or institute who collected a given specimen.

user identifier.description: A user identifier is an identifier provided as part of an authentication process of a client (user) to a service (server). User identifiers normally persist over time, in contrast to session identifiers which are temporary.
