specimen title.description: A specimen (or sample) title should be short and informative. Each specimen title must be unique in a submission.

restricted access.description: A categorical choice recorded when the data for a given measurable datum is available but not shared publicly because of information privacy concerns.

health status trend datum.description: A health status trend is a short-term prognosis about whether health is improving, worsening or unchanging

ITIS.description: The Integrated Taxonomic Information System (ITIS) contains authoritative taxonomic information on plants, animals, fungi, and microbes of North America and the world.

MESH.description: MeSH is the National Library of Medicine's controlled vocabulary thesaurus. It consists of sets of terms naming descriptors in a hierarchical structure that permits searching at various levels of specificity.

NCIT.description: The National Cancer Institute Thesaurus (NCIt) provides reference terminology for many NCI and other systems. It covers vocabulary for clinical care, translational and basic research, and public information and administrative activities.

NIFSTD.description: The NIFSTD ontology of the Neuroscience Information Framework is composed of a collection of OWL modules with separate modules covering major domains of neuroscience: anatomy, cell, subcellular, molecule, organism, function and dysfunction.

SNOMEDCT.description: SNOMED CT is a large clinical health terminology product owned and distributed by SNOMED International.

ASFIS.description: ASFIS is a database curated by the United Nations Food And Agriculture Organization (FAO) Fisheries and Aquaculture Statistics and Information Branch (FIPS). It contains over 12,700 species items selected according to their interest or relation to fisheries and aquaculture.

Wikipedia.description: Wikipedia is a free online encyclopedia that aims to allow anyone to edit articles.

Geonames.description: The GeoNames geographical database covers all countries and contains over eleven million placenames that are available for download free of charge.

EcoLexicon.description: EcoLexicon is a terminological resource developed by the LexiCon Research Group at the University of Granada.

draft IRIDA standard.description: A standard established for use by the Integrated Rapid Infectious Disease Analysis (IRIDA) project, which is a Canadian-led initiative to build an open source, end-to-end platform for infectious disease genomic epidemiology.

ISO3166-1.description: ISO 3166-1 is part of the ISO 3166 standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), and defines codes for the names of countries, dependent territories, and special areas of geographical interest.

ISO3166-2.description: ISO 3166-2 is part of the ISO 3166 standard published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO), and defines codes for identifying the principal subdivisions (e.g., provinces or states) of all countries coded in ISO 3166-1.

ANSI INCITS 38.description: Information Technology – Codes For The Identification Of The States And Equivalent Areas Within The United States, Puerto Rico, And The Insular Areas

NCBI BioSample Pathogen.cl standard.description: A National Center for Biotechnology Information BioSample specification defines fields and terms that provide "descriptions of biological source materials used in experimental assays".

NCBI BioProject standard.description: The National Center for Biotechnology Information BioProject standard is a collection of datums that describe biological data related to a single initiative, originating from a single organization or from a consortium. A BioProject record provides users a single place to find links to the diverse data types generated for that project.

AHA HIPPA standard.description: The American Hospital Association has issued HIPAA Updated Guidelines for Releasing Information on the Condition of Patients

PubMed.description: PubMed comprises more than 26 million citations for biomedical literature from MEDLINE, life science journals, and online books. Citations may include links to full-text content from PubMed Central and publisher web sites.

PulseNet submission standard.description: PulseNet, a national and international surveillance system used to identify and respond to foodborne disease outbreaks, has a standardized laboratory method and data submission standard for pathogen isolate typing test results and related isolate contextual data. From this information clusters of disease can be identified that might represent unrecognized outbreaks.

good health status.description: Good - Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Patient is conscious and comfortable. Indicators are excellent.

fair health status.description: Fair - Vital signs are stable and within normal limits. Patient is conscious, but may be uncomfortable. Indicators are favorable.

serious health status.description: Serious - Vital signs may be unstable and not within normal limits. Patient is acutely ill. Indicators are questionable.

health status history datum.description: A health status history datum is a record of the longer-term pattern or presence of a given patient's health status.

origin.value: (0,0) is the origin of the cartesian coordinate system.
origin.description: A point in zero-dimensional (0D) space in which the origin is a fixed point of reference for the geometry of the surrounding space.

NHS standard.description: United Kingdom National Health Service trusts, boards, etc. have some terminology in common for public disclosure of patient health conditions.

datum status.description: A data item which is about the collection state of a datum at some point in time.

recorded.description: A categorical choice indicating that a datum is available for retrieval.

undetermined health status - awaiting as.description: Patient is awaiting physician and/or assessment.

2D space.description: This data type is for an item that can map to a point, line, set or area on a surface (2 dimensional space) or to the surface itself. It can be a slice of a higher dimensional space. It can be defined by a cartesian or radial coordinate system.

n-dimensional concept.description: This covers the description of data and abstract structure in n-dimensional space. Within space there are coordinate systems, coordinates, and entities made up of coordinates.

latitude specification (ISO 6709).description: A decimal latitude measurement in degrees in conformance with the ISO 6709 standard.

longitude specification (ISO 6709).description: A decimal longitude measurement in degrees in conformance with the ISO 6709 standard.

2D coordinate system.description: A 2D coordinate system is a coordinate system in 2 dimensional space. Each coordinate is composed of an offset from the origin of each dimension

area calculation.description: An area calculation datum is a functional mapping of a two dimensional surface area (can be anything from an abstract polygon, to a postal code or country) to a 1 dimensional scalar. The original surface area may be curved, e.g. spheroid. The surface area can also be described using only one input - for example the radius scalar of a polar coordinate plane described by pi*r^2.

datetime range intermediate.description: A datetime range intermediate datum is a datetime item grouped under a process, and occuring after some process start and before some process end.

significant digits.description: Wikipedia: "The significant figures of a number are digits that carry meaning contributing to its measurement resolution."

datetime set item.description: A datetime set item is a datetime that has been grouped semantically under a given type of process

Canada postal code.description: A Canadian postal code is a postal code that pertains to a geographic region of Canada.

Canada postal code FSA.description: The "Canadia postal code FSA" is the leading FSA (Forward Sortation Area) 3 character portion of a full 6 character Canadian postal code. It can be used to reduce the geographic granularity of a postal code for data generalization or obfuscation.

unordered set.description: An unordered set is a set of elements which have no intrinsic (semantic) order with respect to each other. The set of all living people is not intrinsically ordered; an ordering can only be provided by looking at some partiular feature of the given set elements.

points in 2 dimensions.description: A set of points that exist in a 2-dimensional plane. (This plane may be a cross-section of points defined in n > 2 dimensions).

quadratic surface.description: In Euclidean space, quadrics have dimension D = 2, and are known as quadric surfaces.

spheroid.description: A spheroid, or ellipsoid of revolution, is a quadric surface obtained by rotating an ellipse about one of its principal axes; in other words, an ellipsoid with two equal semi-diameters.

plane.description: In mathematics, a plane is a flat, two-dimensional surface. A plane is the two-dimensional analogue of a point (zero dimensions), a line (one dimension) and three-dimensional space. Planes can arise as subspaces of some higher-dimensional space, as with the walls of a room, or they may enjoy an independent existence in their own right, as in the setting of Euclidean geometry." "When working exclusively in two-dimensional Euclidean space, the definite article is used, so, the plane refers to the whole space.

sequencing instrument model.description: A product name and model number of a manufacturer's genomic (dna) sequencer.

circle.description: A circle is a simple closed shape in Euclidean geometry. It is the set of all points in a plane that are at a given distance from a given point, the centre; equivalently it is the curve traced out by a point that moves so that its distance from a given point is constant.

2D entity.description: A two dimensional entity is an entity composed of one or more points on a two dimensional surface.

library selection.description: Whether any method was used to select for or against, enrich, or screen the material being sequenced.

5-methylcytidine antibody method.description: Selection of methylated DNA fragments using an antibody raised against 5-methylcytosine or 5-methylcytidine (m5C).

Hybrid Selection method.description: Selection by hybridization in array or solution.

PCR method.description: Source material was selected by designed primers.

RANDOM PCR method.description: Source material was selected by randomly generated primers.

RANDOM method.description: Random selection by shearing or other method.

RT-PCR method.description: Source material was selected by reverse transcription PCR

Reduced Representation method.description: Reproducible genomic subsets, often generated by restriction fragment size selection, containing a manageable number of loci to facilitate re-sampling.

cDNA method.description: PolyA selection or enrichment for messenger RNA (mRNA). complementary DNA.

size fractionation method.description: Physical selection of size appropriate targets.

other library method.description: Other library enrichment, screening, or selection process.

library source.description: The library source specifies the type of source material that is being sequenced.

genomic source.description: Genomic DNA (includes PCR products from genomic DNA).

other library source.description: Other, unspecified, or unknown library source material.

transcriptomic source.description: Transcription products or non genomic DNA (EST, cDNA, RT-PCR, screened libraries).

library strategy.description: Sequencing technique intended for this library.

amplicon strategy.description: Sequencing of overlapping or distinct PCR or RT-PCR products. For example, metagenomic community profiling using SSU rRNA

Bisulfite-Seq strategy.description: MethylC-seq. Sequencing following treatment of DNA with bisulfite to convert cytosine residues to uracil depending on methylation status.

DNase-Hypersensitivity strategy.description: Sequencing of hypersensitive sites, or segments of open chromatin that are more readily cleaved by DNaseI.

EST strategy.description: Single pass sequencing of cDNA templates

finishing strategy.description: Sequencing intended to finish (close) gaps in existing coverage.

MBD-Seq strategy.description: Direct sequencing of methylated fractions sequencing strategy.

pool clone strategy.description: Shotgun of pooled clones (usually BACs and Fosmids).

WCS strategy.description: Random sequencing of a whole chromosome or other replicon isolated from a genome.

WGS strategy.description: Random sequencing of the whole genome.

WXS strategy.description: Random sequencing of exonic regions selected from the genome.

library construction protocol.description: Free form text describing the protocol by which the sequencing library was constructed.

library name.description: The submitter's name for this library.

2D boundary.description: A two dimensional boundary is a continuous path (loop) defined on a two dimensional surface.

colony forming unit per 100 milliliter.description: A colony forming unit count which is a count of viable bacterial numbers in 100 milliliters of liquid.

decimal quantity unit.description: A multiplier in the decimal number system that has been applied to an accompanying number or set of numbers often to simplfy their appearance. Numbers described by multipliers may have lost significant digits through rounding or trimming.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis lineage.description: A Mycobacterium tuberculosis lineage is a named family of strains of tuberculosis, named usually with reference to their shared geographic origin.

personal health datum.description: A personal health datum is a datum that pertains to the health situation or history of an individual.

host hospital service status.description: A host hospital service status indicates the state of a host's interaction with hospital medical services.

treated and transferred.description: Received treatment. Transferred to a different facility.

centre point.value: Centre of circle, ellipse or parabola; centre of mass.
centre point.description: A centre point is a point used in the description of an n-dimentional entity from which other (given) aspects of the entity are most efficienty described. A point of symmetry. The entity must have only one such point.

antibiotic resistance not defined.description: A not defined resistance indicates that an isolate was not tested against a given antibiotic, or the result of the test was inconclusive.

MIC dilution measurement datum.description: A MIC test measurement resulting from a laboratory dilution method.

antimicrobial resistance testing method.description: The commercial kit or product used to determine the MIC e.g. E-Test. If a commercial product was not used, include the type of media used.

Etest (device).description: A manual in vitro diagnostic device used by laboratories to determine the MIC (Minimum Inhibitory Concentration) and whether or not a specific strain of bacterium or fungus is susceptible to the action of a specific antimicrobial.

National Institute of Allergy and Infect.description: NIAID provides The GSCID/BRC Project and Sample Application Standard. It is designed to capture standardized human pathogen and vector sequencing metadata to support epidemiologic and genotype-phenotype association studies for human infectious diseases.

RefSeq accession identifier.description: A RefSeq accession identifier is an accession identifier for selected NCBI-curated genomic, transcript and protein sequences. These identifiers are distinct from DDBJ/EMBL/GenBank identifiers.

Genomic Standards Consortium (GSC) stand.description: A Genomic Standards Consortium standard is an international, community-driven standard to facilitate genomic data integration, discovery and comparison.

specimen collection site - geographic fe.description: A landform, biome or built environment at site that a given specimen was collected from.

subject organism.value: A particular human patient, or a given animal or plant.
subject organism.description: An investigative subject which is an organism.

number of passages.description: The number of serial iterations that an isolate is grown in one environment.

passage protocol.description: A passage protocol should detail the number of serial iterations that an isolate is grown in one environment, and the conditions of that environment.

contact specification - specimen related.description: Contact information for an organization related to specimen collection, processing or storage.

draft sequence repository contextual dat.description: This draft specification provides a collection of fields related to the contextual data of a specimen, its genomic sequencing, and its pathogenic epidemiology.

draft sequence repository data - geograp.description: The geographical origin of the sample by city, region, country or latitude and logitude.

draft sequence repository data - antibio.description: A dataset of the minimal inhibitory concentrations (value, unit, sign (<,>, =)) and resistance phenotypes (resistant, sensitive or undetermined) of the sequenced isolate against different antibiotics tested.

draft sequence repository data - virulen.description: The virulence factors determined to be present in the sequenced isolate by phenotypic or target amplification methods e.g. Shiga toxins, hemolysins.

draft sequence repository data - sequenc.description: Measurements or calculated quantities used to assess the extent and success of the sequence assembly process. Metric thresholds are species-specific.

sequencing dna extraction method datum.description: The procedure used to obtain genomic DNA from a sample through chemical, physical or mechanical means.

read paired-end merging software.description: The name and version of the software used to merge paired-end reads before assembly.

read adapter trimming software.description: The name and version of the software product used for removal of adapter sequences from demultiplexed data reads

specimen collection location - state/pro.description: An ontology identifier or textual name of the most precise geographical location available for the site of a specimen collection event.

test drug maximum concentration.description: This is the maximum concentration of a drug applied during an an assay.

test drug minimum concentration.description: A data item which describes the minimum concentration of a drug applied during an an assay

specimen processing organization type.description: An organization related to the collection, isolate production, sequencing or storage of specimen material or data.

draft sequence repository data - food sp.description: This specification offers food source, product type, packaging and processing attributes relevant to describing a food specimen.

isolation medium.description: An isolation medium is a culture medium which has the disposition to encourage growth of particular bacteria to the exclusion of others in the same growth environment.

draft travel log specification.description: This record details a person's travel movement and duration for epidemiological analysis.

draft EBI antimicrobial susceptibility t.description: A standard for European Bioinformatics Institute (EBI) antibiogram data submission

MIC diffusion measurement datum.description: A MIC test measurement resulting from a laboratory diffusion method.

antimicrobial resistance testing referen.description: The version of the antimicrobial reistance testing reference standard protocol used in assessing an isolate.

draft sequence repository data - antibio.description: This is a component of an antibiogram that enables a choice of MIC measurements based on either the diffusion or dilution method. These methods call for different numeric input ranges and units.

feces collection.description: The process of collecting a portion of feces from an organism.

sputum collection.description: The process of collecting a portion of urine from an organism.

rinsing for specimen collection.description: The process of removal and collection of specimen material from the surface of an entity by washing, or a similar application of fluids.

swabbing for specimen collection.description: The process of collecting specimen material using a swab collection device.

exudate collection.description: The process of collecting bodily fluids that have been discharged from blood vessels usually arising from inflammation or injury.

vacuuming for specimen collection.description: The removal or collection of specimen material through the use of suction.

tube containing media or preservative.description: A tube that contains media or preservative

Whirlpak sampling bag.description: A sterilized sampling bag that is puncture proof tabs for protection from damage due to wire-end protrusion and leak-proof closures.

hand scoop.description: A shovel-like utensil that has a deep curved dish and a short handle and is used for digging into a soft substance for lifting out a portion.

vaccum device.description: A device which generates a vacuum to provide suction of material.

draft Enterobase contextual data standar.description: This is a draft (under development) collection of fields for capturing the contextual data for Enterobase (https://enterobase.warwick.ac.uk/) records.

virulence factor name.description: The name of the virulence factor molecule produced by a pathogen that specifically causes disease, or that influences the host's function to allow the pathogen to thrive.

virulence testing protocol name.description: The laboratory protocol used to determine virulence phenotypes and markers.

detection limit.description: The detection limit denotes the smallest measure that can be detected with reasonable certainty for a given analytical procedure.

disease cluster.description: A disease cluster is an unusually high incidence of a particular disease or disorder occurring in close proximity in terms of both time and geography.

infectious disease cluster.description: A disease cluster in which two or more cases have been linked by an infectious disease transmission process.

EBI ENA Webin environmental feature.description: Identifies sequences derived by direct molecular isolation from a bulk environmental DNA sample (by PCR with or without subsequent cloning of the product, DGGE, or other anonymous methods) with no reliable identification of the source organism. Environmental samples include clinical samples, gut contents, and other sequences from anonymous organisms that may be associated with a particular host. They do not include endosymbionts that can be reliably recovered from a particular host, organisms from a readily identifiable but uncultured field sample (e.g., many cyanobacteria), or phytoplasmas that can be reliably recovered from diseased plants (even though these cannot be grown in axenic culture).

EBI European Nucleotide Archive Webin.description: The European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) provides a comprehensive record of the world's nucleotide sequencing information, covering raw sequencing data, sequence assembly information and functional annotation. Webin is an ENA interface and standard for sequence submissions.

breadth of coverage.value: Eighty percent of the reference genome was covered by sequence fragments with a coverage depth of 4X; therefore, the breadth of coverage was 80% (4:5).; Eighty percent of the reference genome was covered by sequence fragments with a coverage depth of 4X; therefore, the breadth of coverage was 80% (4:5).
breadth of coverage.description: A data item which is the amount of a reference sequence covered by a sequence of interest. A data item which is the amount of a reference sequence covered by a sequence of interest.

mean contig length.description: The mean contig length is the count of base pairs in the average size contig of the sequence assembly.

raw sequence data processing datum.description: The procedures used to remove adapters from raw sequence reads, trim low quality bases and where applicable, merge paired-end reads.

specimen strain or isolate identifier.description: Name of strain from which sample was obtained OR name of isolate from which sample was obtained.

latitude and longitude coordinate (NCBI.description: The geographical coordinates of the location where the sample was collected. Specify as degrees latitude and longitude in format "d[d.dddd] N|S d[dd.dddd] W|E", eg, 38.98 N 77.11 W

unsigned integer value specification.description: A 32 bit number having a range 0 - 4294967295.

assembly genome size specification.description: A specification for the size of an assembled genome as measured in base pairs.

date value specification (ISO 8601).description: A date should be recorded as YYYY-MM-DD according to ISO 8601. HOWEVER ... OWL 2.0 does not include xsd:date as a permitted data type, so this value specification only accepts xsd:dateTime

MIC diffusion measurement specification.description: A value specification for a MIC test measurement resulting from a laboratory diffusion method.

MIC dilution measurement specification.description: A value specification for a MIC test measurement resulting from a laboratory dilution method.

subject age specification.description: A value specification which describes the age since birth of a given organism that is involved in an investigation or study at a given time.

boolean value specification.description: A boolean value specification indicates a presence (true value) or absence (false value) of a given feature.

specimen collection site specification.description: A specification for a geographic location that a specimen was collected at.

subject identifier specification.description: A subject identifier specification is a specification including datatype pertaining to a given standard's subject identifier field.

subject disease specification.description: A value specification which describes the name of a disease in a subject that is related to a given investigation, study and/or specimen.

specimen collection site.description: The physical location that a specimen was collected at. The location may be described by geographic coordinates, city or other geopolitical entity, biome, etc.

drug MIC unit specification.description: The unit provided for an antibiotic drug test dosage.

test drug minimum concentration specific.description: A value specification which describes the minimum concentration of a drug applied during an an assay.

travel destination specification.description: A value specification which describes the travel destination a given human has travelled to on a particular trip.

specimen source substance specification.description: A data specification for a specimen source substance, which is an organism substance or food product or environmental substance from which the specimen was extracted.

isolate preparation service.description: An isolate preparation service prepares isolates for molecular sequencing.

critical health status.description: An organism datum about subject health status in which vital signs are unstable and not within normal limits, patient may be unconscious and indicators are unfavorable.

Salmonella subspecies.description: A datum indicating one of six defined subspecies of Salmonella.

PFGE Spel pattern.description: A PFGE pattern resulting from DNA fragmentation induced by the Spel enzyme.

fecal indicator.description: A collection of organisms that is indicative of faecal contamination.

food isolate.description: An isolate derived from a food sample.

microbial 16S RNA typing.description: A method for typing The RNA component of the small (30S) subunit of prokaryotic ribosomes.

Helicos platform.description: A sequencing platform brand provided by Helicos corporation (now defunct).

Ion Torrent platform.description: A sequencing platform provided by the Ion Torrent company.

SOLiD sequening platform.description: A sequencing platform provided by Life Technologies Corporation

rinse.description: Rinse is the liquid output of rinsing plant, animal or other material with liquid with the objective of extracting specimen material from that liquid.

animal rinse.description: Animal rinse is a rinse derived from animal material of one or more animals.

culture plate.description: A low flat-bottomed laboratory container for growing a layer of organisms such as bacteria, molds, and cells on a thin layer of nutrient medium.

fluid from meat rinse.description: A fluid that is obtained from rinsing meat for the purpose of collecting materials and organisms that are on its surface.

BGI Genomics platform.description: A sequencing platform provided by the BGI Genomics company.

MGI platform.description: A sequencing platform provided by the MGI company.

fecal grab.description: A fecal specimen collection method in which feces is obtained by inserting the collection device into the anus of the host, or the feces is captured as it is excreted.

Illumina NextSeq 1000.description: A DNA sequencer which is manufactured by the Illumina corporation using sequence-by-synthesis chemistry that fits on a benchtop and uses P1 and P2 flow cells.

Oxford Nanopore Flongle.description: An adapter for MinION or GridION DNA sequencers manufactured by the Oxford Nanopore corporation that enables sequencing on smaller, single-use flow cells.

stomach content.description: Undigested food material, microbiota, and other materials found in the stomach.

fecal composite.description: A mixture of feces obtained from multiple individuals.

feces (environmental).description: Feces which is deposited in the environment.

box corer.description: A specimen collection device that is used to collect soft sediments in lakes or oceans.

NML lab sample ID.description: A data field which describes a string identifier assigned to a sample or specimen by a laboratory group within the Public Health Agency of Canada’s National Microbiology Laboratory (NML).

NML LabWare sample primary key.description: A numeric sample identifier assigned to a sample or specimen by the Public Health Agency of Canada’s National Microbiology Laboratory (NML) LabWare database. This number is the unique primary key of the NML Labware database SAMPLE table.

RmYN02.description: A severe acute respiratory syndrome-related coronavirus which is 1) bat-derived, 2) sharing 93.3% nucleotide identity with SARS-CoV-2, and 3) contains an insertion at the S1/S2 cleavage site in the spike protein.

cluster/outbreak investigation sampling.description: A sampling strategy in which individuals are chosen for investigation into a disease cluster or outbreak.

diagnostic testing sampling.description: A sampling strategy in which individuals are sampled in the context of diagnostic testing.

research sampling.description: A sampling strategy in which individuals are sampled in order to perform research.

surveillance sampling.description: A sampling strategy in which individuals are sampled for surveillance investigations.

baseline surveillance strategy.description: A surveillance sampling strategy in which baseline is established at the beginning of a study or project by the selection of sample units via random sampling.

targeted surveillance strategy.description: A surveillance sampling strategy in which an aspired outcome is explicity stated.

priority surveillance project strategy.description: A targeted surveillance strategy which is considered important and/or urgent.

screening for Variants of Concern strate.description: A targeted surveillance strategy in which the aim is early detection of variants of concern (VoC) in individuals.

longitudinal surveillance strategy.description: A priority surveillance strategy in which subsets of a defined population can be identified who are, have been, or in the future may be exposed or not exposed - or exposed in different degrees - to a disease of interest and are selected to under go repeat sampling over a defined period of time.

re-infection surveillance strategy.description: A priority surveillance strategy in which a population that previously tested positive for a disease of interest, and since confirmed to have recovered via a negative test, are monitored for positive test indication of re-infection with the disease of interest within a defined period of time.

vaccine escape surveillance strategy.description: A priority surveillance strategy in which individuals are monitored for investigation into vaccine escape, i.e., identifying variants that contain mutations that counteracted the immunity provided by vaccine(s) of interest.

travel-associated surveillance strategy.description: A priority surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history outside of the reporting region within a specified number of days before onset of symptoms.

domestic travel surveillance strategy.description: A travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have an intranational travel history within a specified number of days before onset of symptoms.

international travel surveillance strate.description: A travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history outside of the reporting country in a specified number of days before onset of symptoms.

surveillance of international border cro.description: An international travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history of crossing an international border via air travel or ground transport.
An international travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history of crossing an international border via air travel.
An international travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history of crossing an international border via ground transport.

surveillance from international worker t.description: A travel-associated surveillance strategy in which individuals are selected if they have a travel history outside of the reporting country in a specified number of days before onset of symptoms.

multi-jurisdictional outbreak investigat.description: An outbreak investigation sampling strategy in which individuals are chosen for investigation into a disease outbreak that has connections to two or more jurisdictions.

intra-jurisdictional outbreak investigat.description: An outbreak investigation sampling strategy in which individuals are chosen for investigation into a disease outbreak that only has connections within a single jurisdiction.

viral passage experiment strategy.description: A research sampling strategy in which individuals are sampled in order to perform a viral passage experiment.

protocol testing sampling.description: A research sampling strategy in which samples are collected in order to test a method or protocol.

personal protective gown.description: A personal protective clothing item which is a gown worn in order to provide a barrier between a person and the external environment.

collection cup.description: A device which is used to collect liquid samples.

swab.description: A device which is a soft, absorbent material mounted on one or both ends of a stick. A device which is a soft, absorbent material mounted on one or both ends of a stick.

suprapubic aspiration.description: An aspiration process which involves putting a needle through the skin just above the pubic bone into the bladder to take a urine sample.

tracheal aspiration.description: An aspiration process which collects tracheal secretions.

vacuum aspiration.description: An aspiration process which uses a vacuum source to remove a sample.

air filtration.description: A filtration process which removes solid particulates from the air via an air filtration device.

bronchoalveolar lavage.description: The collection of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BAL) from the lungs.

gastric lavage.description: The administration and evacuation of small volumes of liquid through an orogastric tube to remove toxic substances within the stomach.

saline gargle.description: A collecting specimen from organism process in which a salt water solution is taken into the oral cavity, rinsed around, and gargled before being deposited into an external collection device.

scraping.description: A specimen collection process in which a sample is collected by scraping a surface with a sterile sampling device.

finger prick.description: A collecting specimen from organism process in which a skin site free of surface arterial flow is pierced with a sterile lancet, after a capillary blood droplet is formed a sample is captured in a capillary tupe.

prior antiviral treatment (GENEPIO_01000.description: Antiviral treatment administered prior to the current regimen or test.

washout tear collection.description: A collecting specimen from organism process in which fluid is added to the eye prior to sample collection, effectively "washing out" ocular surface molecules.

virus passage.description: The process of growing a virus in serial iterations.

RNA re-extraction (post RT-PCR).description: A secondary RNA extraction after performing reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The desired output is RNA.

293/ACE2 cell line.description: 293 cells stably expressing the SARS-CoV receptor protein, angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2).

EFK3B cell line.description: Eptesicus fucus (big brown bat) kidney 3B cells.

HRCE cell line.description: Normal human primary renal cortical epithelial cells.

VeroE6/TMPRSS2 cell line.description: VeroE6 cells expressing the transmembrane serine protease TMPRSS2.

hospitalized (non-ICU) datum.description: The condition of being treated as a patient in a hospital without admission to an intensive care unit (ICU).

hospitalized (ICU) datum.description: The condition of being treated as a patient in a hospital intensive care unit (ICU).

medically isolated datum.description: Separation of people with a contagious disease from population to reduce the spread of the disease.

medically isolated (negative pressure) d.description: Medical isolation in a negative pressure environment: 6 to 12 air exchanges per hour, and direct exhaust to the outside or through a high efficiency particulate air filter.

subject age at time of specimen collecti.description: An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 0 to 9 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 10 to 19 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 20 to 29 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 30 to 39 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 40 to 49 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 50 to 59 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 60 to 69 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 70 to 79 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 80 to 89 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be between 90 to 99 years old (inclusive).
An age group that stratifies the age of a case to be greater than or equal to 100 years old.
Age of host at the time of sampling, expressed as an age group in years.

inability to arouse.description: Inability to arouse in response to one or more external stimuli.

cyanotic face.description: Persistent blue discoloration of the lips.

central cyanosis.description: Generalized bluish discoloration of the body and the visible mucous membranes, which occurs due to inadequate oxygenation secondary to conditions that lead to an increase in deoxygenated hemoglobin or presence of abnormal hemoglobin.

cyanotic lips.description: Persistent blue discoloration of the lips.

peripheral cyanosis.description: Bluish discoloration of the distal extremities (hands, fingertips, toes), and can sometimes involve circumoral and periorbital areas. Mucous membranes are generally not involved.

ground glass opacities.description: Focal or diffuse areas of ill-defined, hazy, increased lung attenuation, which cause pulmonary vascular indistinctness, yet through which vessels can still be identified via high-resolution computed tomography or the conventional radiograph.

silent hypoxemia.description: Abnormally low blood oxygen level without the presence of dyspnea/dyspnoea.

pharyngeal exudate.description: Fluid exuded from the pharynx posterior wall.

pseudo-chilblains on fingers.description: Inflammatory chilblain-like nodules on the hands and/or fingers.

pseudo-chilblains on toes.description: Inflammatory chilblain-like nodules on the feet and/or toes.

cardiac injury.description: Trauma to the cardiac muscle or valves.

chronic cough.description: A reflex action of the respiratory tract that is used to clear the upper airways, lasting for more than 8 weeks

chronic gastrointestinal disease.description: A persistent disease that affects the gastrointestinal tract.

postpartum (≤6 weeks).description: The period of time less than or equal to six weeks after labor and delivery.

drug abuse.description: The use of a drug for a reason other than which it was intended or in a manner or in quantities other than directed.

injection drug abuse.description: The use of an injection drug for a reason other than which it was intended or in a manner or in quantities other than directed.

cardiac transplant.description: An individual who is receiving or has received a transplant of a heart.

liver transplant.description: An individual who is receiving or has received a transplant of a liver.

variant of concern (SARS-CoV-2).description: A variant designation which is 1) a variant of the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), 2) believed to have genetic mutations that increase binding affinity to human cells, 3) linked to rapid spread in human populations, and 4) is being monitored.

variant of interest (SARS-CoV-2).description: A variant designation which is 1) a variant of the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), 2) demonstrated to have genetic mutations that increase binding affinity to human cells, 3) linked to rapid spread in human populations, and 4) is under surveillance.

tachyarrhythmia.description: A disorder characterized by an arrhythmia with an above normal rate.

noncardiogenic pulmonary edema.description: A disease process that results in acute hypoxia secondary to a rapid deterioration in respiratory status.Increased capillary permeability and changes in pressure gradients within the pulmonary capillaries and vasculature are mechanisms for which noncardiogenic pulmonary edema occurs. To differentiate from cardiogenic pulmonary edema, pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is not elevated and remains less than 18 mmHg.

neurogenic pulmonary edema.description: A clinical syndrome characterized by the acute onset of pulmonary edema following a significant central nervous system (CNS) insult.

fulminant myocarditis.description: An acute form of myocarditis, whose main characteristic is a rapidly progressive clinical course with the need for hemodynamic support.

complete Kawasaki disease.description: A diagnosis of Kawasaki disease (KD) based on the fulfillment of a set of clinical signs including fever of five or more days' duration with at least four of the following five signs: (i) bilateral conjunctival injection, (ii) cervical lymphadenopathy, (iii) polymorphous skin rash, (iv) changes in the lips or oral mucosa, and (v) changes of the distal extremities.Usual laboratory findings in KD patients include elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein, hypoalbuminemeia, elevated serum hepatic transaminases and leukocytosis with thrombocytosis noted later in the course of the illness.

incomplete Kawasaki disease.description: A diagnosis of Kawasaki disease (KD) when patients fail to meet “classic” clinical features but have laboratory findings usually associated with KD and no reasonable alternate diagnosis, they are said to have incomplete or atypical KD.

acute liver injury.description: A condition of liver damage that is characterized by coagulopathy with no signs of encephalopathy.

ventilation induced lung injury.description: A lung injury that results from mechanical stress and strain that occur during tidal ventilation in the susceptible lung.

muscle injury.description: An injury in muscle tissue caused by bruising, spraining or laceration.

organ failure.description: An organ dysfunction to such a degree that normal homeostasis cannot be maintained without external clinical intervention.

secondary staph infection.description: A infection caused by staphylococcus bacteria, bearing the secondary infection role

secondary strep infection.description: A infection caused by streptococcal bacteria, bearing the secondary infection role

hyperinflammatory shock.description: A systemtic inflammatory response to infectious and/or non-fectious etiologies, resulting in life-threatening, generalized form of acute circulatory failure associated with inadequate oxygen utilization by the cells.

refractory cardiogenic shock.description: A persistent form of cardiogenic shock that presents as persistent tissue hyoperfusion despite administration of adequote doses of vasoactive medications and treatmenft of the underlying aetiology.

refractory cardiogenic plus vasoplegic s.description: A persistent form of cardiogenic shock that presents simultaneously with vasoplegic shock.

fully vaccinated.description: A vaccination status in which an individual has completed a full series of an authorized vaccine according to the regional health institutional guidance.

partially vaccinated.description: A vaccination status in which an individual has started but not yet fully completed a vaccine series authorized and administered according to the regional health institutional guidance.

most probable number per milliliter.description: A unit of microbial density that describes the most probable number of microbes within one milliliter of material.

most probable number per 100 milliliter.description: A unit of microbial density that describes the most probable number of microbes within 100 milliliters of material.

Digital real time polymerase chain react.description: A polymerase chain reaction assay in which a sample is partitioned into many individual reactions, such that target nucleic acid molecules are distributed across partitions and amplified independently, enabling absolute quantification of target sequences based on the proportion of positive reactions, with optional real-time fluorescence monitoring.

third party role.description: A role that inheres in a subject and is realized in processes in which the subject stands in relation to two or more principal parties without being one of those principals, thereby functioning as a third party within that context.

filename.description: A data label which is used to uniquely identify a computer file within a file system.

prior measles infection status.description: A data field which describes the absence or presence of a prior measles infection.

GenapSys sequencing instrument model.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by GenapSys which uses sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and employs electrical-based detection of single nucleotide incorporations. Has CMOS-based detectors, simple fluidics, and no moving parts.

GenapSys GS111.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by GenapSys which uses directCMOS-based impedance detection technology to perform high-accuracy sequencing without optics, suitable for various genomic applications.

GeneMind sequencing instrument model.description: A sequencing instrument manufactured by GeneMind Biosciences Company that performs high-throughput sequencing using sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and fluorescence-based detection.

GeneMind FASTASeq 300.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by GeneMInd which uses high-density flow cells advanced base identification algorithms to perform targeted and whole-genome low-pass sequencing.

GeneMind GenoCare 1600.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by GeneMInd which uses amplication free library preparation and sequencing-by-synthesis to achieve high accuracy sequences.

GeneMind GenoLab M.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by GeneMInd. Uses sequencing-by-synthesis.

Helicos sequencing instrument model.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Helicos which uses glass flow cells and no amplification step. A sequencing run, generates approximately 1,000,000,000 usable reads with a median read length of about 35 nt.

Tapestri sequencing instrument model.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Tapestri which combines microfluidics and targeted sequencing to perform single-cell DNA analysis, enabling high-resolution insights into cellular heterogeneity.

Ultima sequencing instrument model.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ultima Genomics which utilises a traditional flow cell with a massive, open-to-the-elements, flat circular silicon wafer.

Vela sequencing instrument model.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Vela Diagnostics.

Ultima UG100.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Ultima which applies semiconductor sequencing technology for rapid and cost-effective targeted sequencing of human and viral DNA, optimized for clinical laboratory settings.

Vela Sentosa SQ301.description: A DNA sequencer manufactured by Vela which applies semiconductor sequencing technology for rapid and cost-effective targeted sequencing.

Illumina MiSeq i100.description: A DNA sequencer which is manufactured by the Illumina corporation and that is a benchtop model and is designated as part of the MiSeq i100 product series.

Illumina MiSeq i100 Plus.description: A DNA sequencer which is manufactured by the Illumina corporation and that is configured as an enhanced model of the MiSeq i100 Series with support for expanded sequencing capacity relative to the base model.
